A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmegAMP. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, allowing retained, revised, relocated, and removed content to be matched despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v1 reports original classifier and generation experiments, conditioning tests, embedding-regression comparisons, and ID/OOD analyses in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original computational experiments and laboratory MIC measurements for 25 generated peptides against 17 bacterial strains, including resistant strains.

M1.justification: v1's two-channel hydrophobicity/padding representation becomes an embedding using five biochemical scales in v2 Section 3.1. Conditioning changes from full reference-derived vectors to masked-property training, optional attributes, and direct sampling from property ranges. The template-guidance procedure described in v1 is removed.

E1.justification: v2 replaces the generator's AMPlify negative data with 774,405 Peptipedia peptides selected for predicted antibacterial properties. It adds signal/metabolic negative controls, evaluation on Tucker et al.'s experimentally screened sequences, and laboratory testing across 17 strains, including eight MDR strains. Template-constrained generation is no longer evaluated.

E2.justification: v2 adds AMPpredMFA, HydrAMP-AMP, HydrAMP-MIC, SenseXAMP-classifier, and PyAMPA to the classification comparison, and AMP-Diffusion to the generator comparison. New Figure 3 compares reported laboratory success rates with AMP-Diffusion, HydrAMP, CLaSS, and Joker; these are cross-study comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 expands the classification test mixture and adds AUPRC and LR+, replacing v1's HQ-only TPR/FPR evaluation. Generator evaluation switches from amPEPpy to HydrAMP-MIC, redefines diversity, and adds fitness and novelty metrics. Species-conditioned sampling increases from 2,000 to 10,000 peptides. New ablation and laboratory experiments introduce additional sampling and assay protocols.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct generator embedding/scale ablations, single-versus-multiple-property tests, synthetic-negative distribution analyses, external-data robustness evaluation, classifier feature importance, and laboratory backtesting. Synthetic-data ablations are retained with expanded evaluation. v1's embedding-regression, explicit paired ID/OOD, template-matching, and filtering-stage analyses are absent.

E5.justification: Both versions average classifier results over five cross-validation folds. v2 additionally reports independent triplicate MIC assays in Appendix K.1. It does not introduce confidence intervals or a documented significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Classifier and generator results are extensively revised, with additional ablation and external-test results. General-classifier FPR changes from 5.82% to 0.3%, but the evaluation mixture changes, preventing a same-setting improvement interpretation. New Table 16 supports 24/25 peptides active against at least one tested strain at MIC ≤32 µg/mL; v1 has no laboratory results.

T1.justification: v2 introduces a masked conditional-loss formulation and replaces the formal diversity definition based on Levenshtein distance with normalized sequence alignment. Template-guidance derivations are removed. The DDPM/CADS mathematics, classifier weighting, and synthetic-negative N/L! argument are substantially retained or relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add claims of an unprecedented 96% experimental hit rate and potent activity against MDR pathogens. v1's claims concern computational performance, diversity, and filtering. v2 refocuses the contributions on biological embeddings, controllability, and experimentally validated discovery, dropping the separate Rank-filtering contribution.

C2.justification: v2 connects classifier feature importance to charge-mediated membrane interactions and interprets laboratory backtests as supporting specificity. It qualifies external comparisons through differing activity definitions and adds limitations concerning evaluated strains and novel peptide/property spaces. v1's specific template-conflict and ID/OOD failure interpretations disappear.

D1.justification: v2 documents CADS parameters, 276 classifier features and supporting libraries, classifier hyperparameters, early stopping, and laboratory selection/culture/MIC procedures. Reported generator training time changes from 24 to 72 hours, and classifier training time is newly specified. Laboratory peptide sequences are withheld and represented only by identifiers s1–s25.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially rewritten around representations, conditional control, and classifier feature families. New discussion includes AMP-Diffusion, ProT-Diff, protein language models, AMPpredMFA, SenseXAMP, and PyAMPA. Experimental comparisons and synthetic-negative justification also introduce substantial additional literature.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and extensively rewrites the introduction, related work, methods, experiments, and conclusion. Diffusion preliminaries and species-specific classification move into appendices; the main narrative emphasizes embeddings, conditioning, and laboratory validation. The appendix structure is substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: A single-column layout replaces v1's two-column format. Figure 1 is redrawn, conditioning results are reorganized into a combined figure, and the amino-acid frequency plot moves to the appendix. Several v1 analysis figures disappear, while laboratory curves, distribution plots, and numerous new or expanded tables are introduced.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially closes v1's biological-validation gap through triplicate laboratory testing: Table 16 supports activity for 24/25 peptides against at least one of 17 strains. Direct embedding ablations and challenging external controls also strengthen empirical support. Withheld sequences, disagreements between MIC Tables 16–17, and unmatched cross-study comparisons weaken reproducibility and precise superiority claims, but the central laboratory validation represents a substantial overall gain.
